Don't send one of these twerps.|Han Solo|audio=Solo-Twerps.flac|}} '''Beedo''' was a [[Rodian]] who was under [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]'s [[Jabba's criminal empire|employ]] on [[Tatooine]]. Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin]], Beedo accompanied Jabba to [[Docking Bay 94]] in [[Mos Eisley]] and was near the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' as Jabba and the [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]] conversed. The Rodian was then present in [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]] in [[4 ABY]] when a group of Solo's comrades tried to [[Rescue of Han Solo|rescue]] Solo, who had been frozen in [[carbonite]] and displayed as a decoration in the [[Hutt]]'s throne room. After Beedo witnessed the [[Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker]] slay Jabba's pet [[rancor]] [[Pateesa]], the crime lord ordered that the prisoners be executed at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]]; however, Solo and his allies managed to ultimately kill Jabba and escape. ==Biography== ===Hunt for Solo=== {{Quote|Blast!''"
"''How many?|Senni and Brea Tonnika abandon their plan after seeing Beedo and his companions|audio=Tonnikas-Blast.flac|{{StoryCite|story=You Owe Me a Ride|book=From a Certain Point of View}}}} [[File:Jabbathehutt94.png|thumb|right|300px|Beedo (second from left) accompanied Jabba to Docking Bay 94.]] A mysterious [[Rodian]]{{SideshowCite|set=Sixth Scale Figures|pack=Beedo|link=collectibles/star-wars-beedo-sideshow-1004892|archivedate=20250726142241}} from the [[planet]] [[Rodia]], Beedo was a figure of which little was known, although he was rumored to [[Jabba's criminal empire|work]] as a [[bounty hunter]] for the [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] during the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. In [[1 BBY]],{{FilmDate|IV|1}} Beedo accompanied{{StarWarsShow|jo3E0Z0BXEE|Star Wars: The Clone Wars Coming to SDCC, Comedian Paul F. Tompkins, and More!|sw_url=video/star-wars-the-clone-wars-coming-to-sdcc-comedian-paul-f-tompkins-and-more}} two other Rodians, the bounty hunter [[Boba Fett]], three other [[human]]s including [[Ront Byrnloo]],{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/853330463041232897|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Two newly named cantina denizens courtesy of the panel @TomSpinaDesigns and I just wrapped. #SWCO|archivefile=File:RontByrnlooTwitter.png}} and Jabba to [[Docking Bay 94]] in [[Mos Eisley]] [[spaceport]] on the planet [[Tatooine]] in search of the [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]]. Solo had dumped a shipment of [[spice]] belonging to Jabba, which caused the Hutt to place a [[bounty]] on him. The group found no sign of Solo himself, but did discover his [[YT-1300 light freighter|freighter]], the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''. As they poked around beneath the ''Falcon'', the sisters [[Brea Tonnika|Brea]] and [[Senni Tonnika]] sneaked in the back of the [[Hangar|docking bay]] intending to [[Thief|steal]] the ''Falcon''. Hpowever, upon seeing Beedo and the other thugs with Jabba, the pair abandoned their plan and left to look for a different [[starship]]. Solo then arrived in the docking bay, having just [[Death|killed]] Beedo's cousin, [[Greedo]], another bounty hunter in Jabba's employ. Solo greeted Jabba, causing the thugs to spin and aim their [[blaster]]s at the smuggler, but he soon managed to work out a deal with the Hutt based on a new job he had just taken, so the crime lord called off Beedo and his comrades and they left the docking bay alongside their employer. ===At the palace=== [[4 ABY|Four years later]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|VI}} to [[4 ABY]]. Beedo was one of two Rodians present in [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]] when the [[droid]]s [[C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2]] arrived bearing a message from the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]]. As the pair entered the Hutt's throne room, both Rodians were stood to the left of the door interacting with a control panel. When R2-D2 then projected the [[Hologram|holographic]] form of Skywalker, Beedo turned to listen to the [[Jedi]]'s message. Skywalker asked that Jabba considered freeing Solo, who had failed to repay Jabba for the lost spice and been frozen in [[carbonite]] for display in the Hutt's throne room. When the message ended, Jabba announced he would keep Solo where he was, earning laughter from the court.{{Film|VI}} Beedo later stood in the doorway of the throne room and danced alongside a [[Jawa]] as the [[Max Rebo Band]]''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' performed the song [[Jedi Rocks]] for the court. When the song ended, the crime lord demanded the band play an encore; however, the second performance abruptly ended when the [[Twi'lek]] dancer [[Oola]] refused Jabba's advances and so was dropped into a pit beneath the throne room to be [[Diet|eaten]] by [[Pateesa]], the Hutt's pet [[rancor]]. Beedo and the Jawa wereamong the court members who rushed forward to watch her demise, but afterwards turned in surprise as the sound of [[blaster]] fire came from outside the room. ===Trouble arrives=== [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]], disguised as the bounty hunter [[Boushh]], then entered the courtroom leading the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]] in chains. Beedo and the Jawa returned to the entryway and watched as Jabba and "Boushh" negotiated over a bounty that the Hutt had placed on Chewbacca. However, Organa was unsatisfied with the amount the crime lord was offering and produced a [[thermal detonator]] in order to threaten him into paying more. As many courtiers cowered in fear, Jabba laughed and offered the princess a compromise that satisfied her. Beedo, who had retreated further back into the entryway, then watched as Chewbacca was dragged away. [[File:Luke-DL18.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Luke Skywalker threatened Jabba in front of Beedo and the rest of the court.]] That night Organa snuck back into the room to free Solo. She succeeded in freeing him from the carbonite, but the pair were caught by Jabba, who had laid in wait in order to catch Organa in the act. After Skywalker arrived to [[Rescue of Han Solo|free his friends]], Beedo stood near. the [[Ishi Tib]] [[Shasa Tiel]] in a crowd that gathered around the Jedi in the throne room as he made demands of Jabba. When Skywalker threatened the Hutt with a [[DL-18 blaster pistol|blaster]], Beedo and Tiel retreated to the throne room's entryway before Jabba dropped Skywalker and the [[Gamorrean]] [[Jubnuk]]''[[Star Wars: Complete Locations, New Edition]]'' into the rancor pit. As Jabba and the court watched, Pateesa consumed Jubnuk before being slain by Skywalker. Outraged, Jabba ordered Skywalker, Solo and Chewbacca be brought before him, and Beedo stood near the stairs leading to the palace's [[prison]] as the [[prisoner]]s were brought up. The Hutt decreed that the trio would be taken to the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]] and fed to the [[sarlacc]] there as an alternate means of execution. Jabba and many of his courtiers then traveled to the pit to witness the execution, but Skywalker and his comrades managed to escape and kill Jabba in the process. ==Personality and traits== Beedo was a mysterious Rodian of unclear motives. In addition to having black [[eye]]s, he had a [[Color|green]], scaly skin and the reptilian [[antenna]]e typical of his species. Even though he was able to maintain a secretive persona, his skin and antennae served to make him stand out amongst Jabba's court. Rather than join in the musical celebrations held before Jabba's throne and above the rancor pit, Beedo preferred to relax on the stairway. ==Equipment== Beedo made use of a [[DT-12 heavy blaster pistol]]. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|Greedo, by far, is the most infamous of all Rodians, but he wasn't the only one of his kind working for Jabba. There's Beedo, the docking bay Rodian who is coincidentally wearing an identical green jumpsuit, a popular Rodian fashion choice for sure… well, unless you're Greeata.|The narrator in ''The Star Wars Show''|{{StarWarsShow|jo3E0Z0BXEE|Star Wars: The Clone Wars Coming to SDCC, Comedian Paul F. Tompkins, and More!|sw_url=video/star-wars-the-clone-wars-coming-to-sdcc-comedian-paul-f-tompkins-and-more}}}} The character that would eventually be identified as Beedo first appeared in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], in which three identically costumed Rodians appear in a scene filmed between Friday, [[April 9]], and Thursday, [[April 22]], [[1976]], on stage 3 at [[Elstree Studios]].''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]'' The scene was cut from the original 1977 release, but later included as part of the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] re-release of the film in [[1997]]. [[Marolyn Turk]] then portrayed Beedo{{SW|url=news/star-wars-in-the-uk-memorabilia-23-24-november-2013|text=Star Wars in the UK: Memorabilia, 23-24 November 2013}} in the [[1983]] original trilogy film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. The Jabba's throne room scenes were filmed over three weeks on Stage 8 at [[Elstree Studios]] between [[January 25]] and [[February 11]], [[1982]].''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]'' The character's costume re-used a jacket worn by the [[Gender|female]] [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebel]] personnel in [[Echo Base]] in the [[1980]] original trilogy film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']],{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-9-things-you-might-not-know-about-rodians|text=Much to Learn You Still Have: 9 Things You Might Not Know About Rodians}} one of who Turk also portrayed. Due to how hot the costumes were, the actors were cooled with hair dryers inserted through the masks' mouthes, but according to Turk this resulted in everyone becoming ill with sore throats and colds and so the practice was stopped.{{WebCite|url=https://www.jedinews.com/interviews/articles/sci-fi-central-marolyn-turk-2-star-wars-films|text=Sci-Fi Central: Marolyn Turk In 2 ''Star Wars'' Films|author=[[Mark Newbold|Newbold, Mark]]|date=2016-09-2|archivedate=20201108144645}} In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the name Beedo was first used in "Much to Learn You Still Have: 9 Things You Might Not Know About Rodians," a [[StarWars.com]] article written by [[Dana Jennings]] and published on [[July 29]], [[2016]]. The article only covered the Rodian appearing in ''Return of the Jedi''{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-9-things-you-might-not-know-about-rodians|text=Much to Learn You Still Have: 9 Things You Might Not Know About Rodians}} who was first identified as such in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity on a card in the [[1983 Topps Star Wars: Return of the Jedi Series 1|1983 Topps ''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' Series 1]] set of cards released by [[Topps]] in [[1983]].{{Topps|set=1983 Topps Star Wars: Return of the Jedi Series 1|cardname=Beedo and a Jawa|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/72969/cid/5256869}} The one hundred and first episode of ''[[The Star Wars Show]]'' video series, released on [[June 27]], [[2018]], then identified the ''A New Hope'' Rodian as also being Beedo, a connection that was not made in Legends. ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Beedo}} *{{Film|IV}} {{1st}} {{Ret}} *''[[Star Wars: A New Hope Cinestory Comic]]'' *{{Film|VI}} *[[Return of the Jedi Read-Along Storybook and CD|''Return of the Jedi'' Read-Along Storybook and CD]] ==Sources== *''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]'' {{BtsOnly}} *{{SW|url=news/star-wars-in-the-uk-memorabilia-23-24-november-2013|text=Star Wars in the UK: Memorabilia, 23-24 November 2013}} {{BtsOnly}} *''[[Star Wars Costumes: The Original Trilogy]]'' {{Po}} *{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-9-things-you-might-not-know-about-rodians|text=Much to Learn You Still Have: 9 Things You Might Not Know About Rodians}} {{1stID|Beedo}} *[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] {{Po}} *''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' *{{StarWarsShow|jo3E0Z0BXEE|Star Wars: The Clone Wars Coming to SDCC, Comedian Paul F.
